instruction: Add a 4th professor entry in the spreadsheet: No. 4, Professor 'Jiayi Pan', University 'UCSD', Major 'Computer Science'.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened professor homepages in Chrome, read email info, switched back to LibreOffice Calc, and entered email addresses. However, the entered emails did not match the gold standard, resulting in score 0.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate URLs in Chrome, switch between Chrome and LibreOffice Calc, read webpage content, type values into spreadsheet cells
metadata.failure_analysis: Model entered incorrect email addresses that did not match the gold reference file. The compare_table evaluator found mismatches in the sheet data.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to adding a new row with explicit given values. This tests the model's demonstrated ability to click on cells and type values in the correct row/column positions, without web research.
metadata.explanation: Task requires adding a new professor entry in row 6 (next empty row after existing 3 entries in rows 3-5). Evaluator reads cells A6, B6, C6, D6 and checks each matches the expected value. Partial credit: 0.25 per correct column.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads row 6, columns A-D from the xlsx file, matching the expected location of the 4th professor entry (rows 3-5 have existing entries)
Metric correctly handles expected parameter: expected.type='rule' so expected IS the rules dict, and metric accesses expected.get('expected_row', {}) which is correct
Case-insensitive comparison with strip() is appropriate for text cell values
Partial credit scoring (0.25 per correct column out of 4) is well-designed for this multi-field task
Postconfig properly activates the LibreOffice window and saves (Ctrl+S) before getter reads, ensuring fresh file state
All 4 instruction requirements are verified: No. (A6='4'), Professor (B6='Jiayi Pan'), University (C6='UCSD'), Major (D6='Computer Science')
